cases.case: P1 retained inner identity plus prior-record preservation
cases.shape: Use a current-token-bound fake with one fd9-closed inner session that outlives its runner; seed old holder and fallback SELF_HOLD records before launch. Confirm the new launcher has actually observed the inner SID, then make its inner attempts evidence unreadable, require typed unknown plus the same retained SID and a live excluded holder, restore only that obstacle, and require positive outer/inner-empty recovery. Assert byte-preserved prior identity/fallback contents in their named prior destinations.
cases.ordering_correction: Section 7 says 'unreadable before the census' while expecting a retained SID; before its first successful discovery the launcher cannot already know that SID. For the retention assertion, place the fault after an acknowledged census containing that SID; a pre-discovery read failure should instead assert unknown without inventing a retained identity. [Union semantics](frozen-inputs/launch-s5-setup-exclusion.v3.sh#L185) [Proposal wording](frozen-inputs/FINDINGS_MAP_AND_REQUEST_V3.md#L54)

cases.case: P2 failed corrective receipt and recovery
cases.shape: Use a current-bound fake returning 0 and a narrow acknowledged fault that allows the first receipt, then fails the RELEASED holder update and its corrective receipt. Require retained SELF-HOLD, separate raw=observed 0, both publication causes, and no successful launcher termination; repair the exact obstacle and require eventual final_rc=90 with corrected retained receipt.
cases.readiness_detail: The fault must target the ordering between adjacent publication operations deterministically; a sleep followed by chmod is not proof of that branch. The packet supplies a scenario, not an implemented supported fault seam, so this is a control-preparation detail, not a demand to change the launcher or build a general harness. [Publication order](frozen-inputs/launch-s5-setup-exclusion.v3.sh#L197) [Proposal](frozen-inputs/FINDINGS_MAP_AND_REQUEST_V3.md#L54)
